intent: Test whether maximum lookahead (y=0.08 m) plus a wider track (0.13 m) and a larger wheel (0.04 m) can cut the overshoot seen in iteration 2 and convert the oval and slalom runs into completions, while keeping the seven-sensor array unchanged so the Integrator's controller work carries over.
learning: Next iteration, check: (a) whether steering_oscillation falls below the 0.27 seen in iteration 2, which would confirm that the wider track adds useful damping; (b) whether max_error on the s-bend still reaches 0.06 m, which would mean turn authority is now the limit and the track should come back toward 0.11 m; (c) whether completion_time drops on the oval with the 0.04 m wheel, measured against the 3 s limit; (d) whether progress on the slalom improves at y=0.08 m. Ask the Integrator whether the outer sensors at x=±0.03 m still give a usable signal at the far edge of the line, and whether the signal saturates at maximum lookahead.
rationale: Iteration 2 is the best design so far (score 171.3), and the evidence shows which changes helped. Progress on the oval rose from about 0.15 to 0.63, and 2 of 20 oval trials finished, so moving the sensors to y=0.07 m, widening the array to 7 sensors, and raising wheel_radius to 0.035 m all helped. Every run still ends off_track, and max_error sits at the 0.06 m floor. The new signal is the jump in steering_oscillation (0.27 to 0.28, from about 0.10 to 0.13 before) and control_effort (about 8 to 8.5, up from about 2.6 to 4.2), which points to a response that is now too aggressive and overshoots. The track was widened to 0.11 m, but the robot still turns too sharply for the s-bend and slalom. Body width cannot help: the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at the 0.06 m floor across the allowed body widths. Changes in this proposal: (1) move the sensors further forward from y=0.07 to y=0.08 m, the top of the allowed range, for more lookahead, since lookahead has been the strongest positive lever so far; (2) widen wheel_track from 0.11 to 0.13 m, which lowers the turn rate per unit of wheel differential and adds damping against the overshoot; (3) raise wheel_radius from 0.035 to 0.04 m for more ground speed, because completion needs roughly 1.5 m/s and no run has come close. Mass (0.6 kg) and body_length (0.14 m) stay the same. Expected result: lower steering_oscillation and control_effort, more progress on the s-bend and slalom, and more oval completions. The main risk is that the wider track slows the turn response enough to cause off_track on the sharpest bends, which I will check with max_error on the s-bend.
